Chicken marinated in jerk, cooked on the grill or low and slow in the oven
40-45 minutes on the grill, or about 1½ hours in the oven
grill, or a baking tray and tinfoil
chicken pieces, or a whole chicken
Score the chicken skin with a sharp knife, cutting the skin but not into the meat.
Be sure that marinade gets into every little crevice of the meat. Anywhere from 2 to 4 hours is good and up to 36 hours is ideal.
On the grill: cook for 40-45 mins to reach a cooking temp and a crispy skin. If you're cooking a whole chicken, cook breast side down and baste with the jerk sauce every 10 mins.

In the oven, for a juicy low n' slow cooked chicken that will impress: preheat your oven to 160°C. Place the chicken in a baking tray, make sure to cover the chicken with the left over marinade, and cover with tinfoil.
Cook for 1 hour until the chicken is cooked the whole way through.
Remove the tinfoil and turn up the heat to 220°C until the skin is brown and crispy.
Allow the chicken to rest for 10 mins.
Take the remaining liquid from the baking tray and put into a saucepan with some tomato paste and a little cornflour to thicken.
Pour sauce over chicken. Serve with a fresh salad. Use your hands.
The booklet says both 230°C and 220°C for crisping the skin; either works.
Source: Lil Portie Homemade, the recipe booklet from Lil Portie Caribbean Kitchen.
